requirements.title: The web application shall display its name and semantic version in the application footer, matching the version field in package.json

vision.paraphrase: The app must demonstrate version transparency as part of its design discipline. This requirement supports the reference-implementation goal by making the version source single and visible.
Version display reinforces the principle of transparency in how the app communicates its operational state and code provenance to end users and reference-readers alike.

conops.paraphrase: The version footer provides immediate context that the user is running a real, versioned application from the moment they first open it.

requirements.title: The web application shall emit a log line on application startup containing its name and semantic version at INFO level, in human-readable plain text

vision.paraphrase: This requirement embodies the reference-implementation goal of making the codebase's lifecycle visible and debuggable for developers who read it end-to-end.

conops.paraphrase: The startup log message signals to developers that the app has initialized and is ready to serve the user, establishing confidence in the system's operational state.

requirements.title: The web application shall display guidance text and an add-habit input when the active habits list is empty

vision.paraphrase: This supports the zero-friction habit creation goal by presenting the user with clear next-step guidance and an input field immediately, removing confusion on first use.
Guidance text in empty states aligns with the design principle of avoiding blank screens and providing helpful instruction rather than leaving users uncertain.

conops.paraphrase: The empty-state guidance and add-habit input are the first interactive elements the user sees when opening the app, welcoming them to begin tracking.

requirements.title: The web application shall display guidance text when the archived habits list is empty

vision.paraphrase: Clear guidance text in empty archived states prevents user confusion and communicates that archiving is a working feature, even when no habits are currently archived.

conops.paraphrase: When a user switches to the Archived view, clear guidance text confirms they have no archived habits, making the system's behavior predictable and transparent.

requirements.title: The web application shall render a functional habit-list UI at a mobile viewport width

vision.paraphrase: The requirement for mobile responsiveness aligns with the design principle that users often check in on habits via phone, making mobile usability essential for the core loop.

conops.paraphrase: On mobile, the add-habit input and done-today control must remain clickable and discoverable, enabling the habit check-in experience on the device users carry everywhere.

requirements.title: The web application shall render a functional habit-list UI at a desktop viewport width

vision.paraphrase: Full responsiveness across desktop and mobile ensures the app is equally usable across all devices and form factors, supporting the minimalist, single-screen design principle.

conops.paraphrase: On desktop, the habit list and controls scale gracefully to take advantage of the larger screen while maintaining the single-screen, above-the-fold design principle.

requirements.title: The web application shall present the add-habit input, the active/archived filter, and the habit list on a single page with no separate navigation pages

vision.paraphrase: The design direction calls for a minimalist, single-screen layout with no navigation menu beyond the active/archived toggle, keeping the entire core loop reachable without leaving the page.

conops.paraphrase: The proposed system description frames the browser tab as the only runtime, implying all core interactions happen on one continuously-updating view rather than across separate pages.
